skill.name: creative-portfolio-resume
skill.description: Plan creative resumes with separate ATS-compatible and designed versions, role-specific content, visual specifications, and portfolio links.
skill.summary: Create a two-version resume strategy that balances clear application content with a consistent creative identity.
skill.author: paramchoudhary

security_audit.summary: All seven static findings are false positives: five identify Markdown fences, and two identify ordinary resume layout guidance. No evidence found of executable commands, system reconnaissance, data exfiltration, or prompt injection in SKILL.md.

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 204-206 enclose a plain portfolio address in a Markdown fence. This is display text, not Ruby or shell execution.
Line 206 closes the portfolio example, while line 209 opens the next example. The intervening heading contains no command or execution instruction.
Lines 209-212 fence a sample resume achievement and case study address. These are resume content examples, not executable shell syntax.
Line 212 closes a Markdown example, and line 275 opens a Markdown output template. The intervening content provides design checklists and software recommendations.
Lines 275-318 contain a fenced Markdown resume strategy template with headings and placeholders. No Ruby code, shell command, or execution request appears.
Lines 73-74 introduce resume formatting elements to avoid, starting with multiple columns. This concerns document layout, not inspection of a computer system.
Lines 241-242 ask whether resume elements align to a grid and achieve visual balance. These are design checks, not system reconnaissance instructions.

content.user_title: Plan Creative Resumes and Portfolio Integration
content.value_statement: Creative resumes can lose readability when visual design conflicts with application software. This skill guides separate application and portfolio versions with clear content and consistent branding.
actual_capabilities: Recommend when to use an ATS-compatible resume or a designed portfolio version.
Provide typography, color, spacing, margin, and visual hierarchy guidance.
Tailor resume recommendations for designers, marketers, writers, photographers, and video professionals.
Suggest portfolio links, case study references, and website resume options.
Structure a resume strategy with version choices, design specifications, portfolio integration, and content adjustments.
Provide design checklists for readability, accessibility, print appearance, and brand consistency.
limitations: Provides written guidance and templates, not a bundled document generator or design application.
Does not test resumes against actual applicant tracking systems or guarantee parsing compatibility.
Does not include automated PDF, DOCX, or portfolio website export tooling.
Requires your career facts, portfolio links, and target role to produce specific recommendations.

use_cases.title: Prepare Application and Networking Versions
use_cases.description: Plan a clean application resume and a designed networking version with consistent typography and portfolio links.

use_cases.title: Connect Experience to Case Studies
use_cases.description: Organize product design experience around clear achievements and relevant portfolio case studies.

use_cases.title: Align Resume and Personal Brand
use_cases.description: Develop readable resume content and restrained visual specifications that match a writing portfolio.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Resume Format
prompt_templates.prompt: I am a [creative role] applying through [application channel]. Recommend a resume version and explain the key layout choices.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: decide between an application resume and a designed version.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Creative Resume
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my resume for [target role]: [resume text and layout description]. Flag readability, ATS formatting, and portfolio integration issues.

prompt_templates.title: Specify Two Resume Versions
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan ATS-compatible and designed resumes for [role] in [industry]. Use [experience], [portfolio URL], and [brand preferences]. Specify typography, colors, layout, and content adjustments.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: develop a complete two-version resume strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Resume and Portfolio
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [resume], [case study summaries], and [brand guidelines] to plan versions for [application channels]. Recommend portfolio placement, website resume options, and a final design checklist.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate resume content, visual identity, and portfolio presentation.

output_examples.input: A graphic designer needs an online application resume and a version for direct agency outreach.
output: Application version: use a single column, standard headings, and a clearly written portfolio address.
Direct outreach version: use consistent brand accents, a readable type hierarchy, and a prominent portfolio link.
Keep experience details consistent between versions and check text readability before sending.

output_examples.input: A product designer wants to connect a checkout redesign project to a portfolio case study.
output: Describe the checkout redesign with your verified contribution and measurable result.
Place a clearly labeled case study link beside the relevant project.
Keep the application version simple and use the designed version to reflect your portfolio identity.

best_practices: Use separate application and designed versions, and keep their career facts synchronized.
Provide verified achievements, target roles, and relevant portfolio links before requesting tailored guidance.
Review readability, link accuracy, color contrast, and printed appearance before sharing a resume.
anti_patterns: Submitting a heavily designed, multicolumn resume to an application portal without checking its requirements.
Replacing clear achievements with decorative graphics, skill bars, or vague claims.
Treating general ATS guidance as proof that every application system will parse the document correctly.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It guides a written resume strategy covering application and designed versions, visual specifications, portfolio links, and role-specific content.

faq.question: Does it guarantee ATS compatibility?
faq.answer: No. It recommends conservative formatting but does not run parsing tests against actual applicant tracking systems.

faq.question: Can it generate finished PDF or DOCX files?
faq.answer: The skill includes guidance and a Markdown strategy template, not export tooling. Finished documents require a suitable editor or separate tools.

faq.question: Which creative roles does it cover?
faq.answer: It includes guidance for graphic designers, UX and product designers, marketing professionals, writers, photographers, and video professionals.

faq.question: Can I use one resume for every channel?
faq.answer: The skill recommends a simple application version and a designed version for portfolio use, networking, or direct submissions.

faq.question: What should I provide before using it?
faq.answer: Provide your target role, application channel, accurate experience, portfolio links, and any existing brand preferences.
